response.sql: WITH d AS (SELECT a.district_id AS district_id, di.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS client_count FROM disp dp JOIN account a ON a.account_id = dp.account_id JOIN district di ON di.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY a.district_id, di.A3) SELECT district_id, region, client_count, CAST(client_count AS REAL) / SUM(client_count) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS share_of_region, CAST(client_count AS REAL) / SUM(client_count) OVER () AS share_of_total FROM d ORDER BY share_of_total DESC, district_id LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each disp row is counted once as one client-account link (COUNT(*) of disp records, as the request states), so a client linked to several accounts in the same district is counted multiple times; the district is the account's branch district, not the client's own district.
Region and overall totals are computed over all districts (not just the top 10), and ties in share are broken by district_id.
